CheckTitle: Ensure IAM policies do not grant full CloudTrail management access
Description: IAM policies (customer-managed and inline) must not grant unrestricted CloudTrail access (cloudtrail:*). Full CloudTrail access enables deletion of trails, stopping of logging, and modification of log configuration — actions that directly undermine audit integrity.
Risk: Full CloudTrail access allows an attacker to delete trails, stop logging, or modify the log destination — eliminating the audit record of their actions. Audit trail destruction is a documented post-compromise technique used to cover attacker activity.
Remediation: Replace cloudtrail:* permissions with only the specific read actions required (e.g., cloudtrail:GetTrailStatus, cloudtrail:LookupEvents). Protect CloudTrail modification permissions using SCPs that restrict cloudtrail:DeleteTrail and cloudtrail:StopLogging.
SeverityBasis: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AU-9 (Protection of Audit Information), AU-2 (Event Logging). Full CloudTrail control enables direct audit evasion. Severity is assigned by the framework's three-tier classification model defined in docs/severity_classification_model.md.
AuthoritativeSource: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5; AWS CloudTrail documentation — Best practices for CloudTrail
CISControl: N/A — CloudTrail permission scoping is not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0 IAM controls
ThreatReference: MITRE ATT&CK for Cloud T1562.008 (Disable or Modify Cloud Logs)
